report.source_text: The CT images revealed a large heterogeneous enhancing mass measuring 22.5×16.5×22.5 cm in the right lower hemithorax. The mass did not involve the rib cage but exerted pressure on the adjacent lung and cardiomediastinal structures, including the superior vena cava, right atrium, and right pulmonary vein. A large pleural fibroma was hypothesized based on these findings (Fig. 2). CT scan did not show any adenopathy, other mass lesions, or bone metastasis.

report.source_text: Consequently, the patient underwent a right posterolateral open thoracotomy for mass resection. The tumor, originating from the anterior mediastinum, was located within the right lung. A portion of the lower lobe of the right lung was resected. The encapsulated mass measured 25.3×19×17 cm and weighed 3720 g (Fig. 4).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Doege-Potter syndrome (solitary fibrous tumor causing non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old male presented with recurrent fasting hypoglycemia (20-50 mg/dL) manifesting as sweating, tremors, and weakness over two months. Biochemical evaluation during hypoglycemia (glucose 25 mg/dL) revealed non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia with inappropriately low insulin (1 microIU/mL), C-peptide (<0.5 microg/L), and suppressed IGF-1 (60 mcg/L, below 1st percentile), consistent with NICTH. CT imaging identified a large 22.5×16.5×22.5 cm heterogeneous enhancing mass in the right lower hemithorax compressing mediastinal structures. Histopathological examination confirmed solitary fibrous tumor (pleural fibroma) with spindle cells positive for CD34, STAT6, and Bcl-2, and negative for mesothelial markers (S100, CK7, WT1, D2-40, calretinin, MDM2). The patient underwent right posterolateral thoracotomy with complete resection of the encapsulated 25.3×19×17 cm, 3720g mass and partial right lower lobectomy. Post-operatively, serum glucose normalized, hypoglycemic episodes resolved, dyspnea resolved, and chest radiograph at two weeks demonstrated pulmonary re-expansion.
